requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: The executor created vgdata/lvdata, formatted it as XFS, and directly observed it mounted read-write at /srv/data. The final post-restart observation again showed the active logical volume mounted at that path.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted, preserving its contents.
requirements.summary: The mount ID remained 118 across the resize, directly demonstrating that /srv/data stayed mounted. The logical volume and XFS filesystem grew from 1 GiB to 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes), and the sentinel file retained the same SHA-256 hash and content. Post-restart checks reconfirmed the final size and intact data.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence. node1 has a 2 GiB XFS logical volume mounted at /srv/data; it was expanded online without changing the mount identity or altering its contents. The independent restart protocol also fully demonstrated persistence and healthy recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a clear role: creating the backing PV/VG, LV, filesystem and proof content; performing the online extension; configuring persistence; and executing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The two timeout results occurred while the scheduled reboot made the node temporarily unreachable and show no separate mutation. After execution there were no failed services, new listening endpoints, package-health problems, or unexplained temporary-file residue. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, storage, mount, and data state, independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
